title: Global finite length for a fraction-field submodule
statement: Let R be a domain with fraction field K, and let M be an R-submodule of K^{\oplus r} for a nonnegative integer r. If R is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension 1 [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], then for every nonzero x in R the R-module M/xM has finite length [def-weil-pbc-module-length].

proof.text: If x is a unit, then xM=M and M/xM=0, which has finite length. Thus assume x is a nonunit.

Let S be the finite set of maximal ideals containing x, supplied by [lem-sc-finite-maximals-over-element]. For each m in S, localization gives the Noetherian local domain R_m, preserves the fraction field K, and preserves the dimension-one prime-chain bound; M_m is an R_m-submodule of K^{\oplus r}. The local finite-length theorem [lem-weil-pbc-dim-one-submodule-quotient-finite-length] therefore gives finite length of M_m/xM_m.

Put Q=M/xM. It is killed by x, so Q_m=0 for every maximal ideal m outside S. If N is a nonzero subquotient of Q, choose a nonzero element of N; its annihilator is proper and is contained in some maximal ideal m, and x in that maximal ideal, so m lies in S. Hence every strict inclusion in a chain of submodules of Q remains strict after localization at at least one m in S.

For each m in S, localization sends a chain of submodules of Q to a chain in Q_m. Given a strict chain N_0 subsetneq ... subsetneq N_k in Q, step 3 chooses for each index i a maximal ideal m(i) in S where N_{i-1,m(i)} subsetneq N_{i,m(i)} remains strict. For a fixed m, the indices with m(i)=m form a strictly increasing subchain after localization, so their number is at most length_{R_m}(Q_m), finite by step 2. Summing over the finite set S bounds k by the sum of these local lengths. Hence every chain in Q has bounded finite length, so Q=M/xM has finite length.
